name: tdd
purpose: Make broken behavior executable before fixing a bug with a clear cheap test path, then prove the focused regression test passes.
triggers: User explicitly asks for TDD, a failing test, or a regression test.
A bug has an obvious cheap local test target; skip unclear, expensive, integration-heavy or unrequested test paths.
inputs: Intended and current bug behavior, affected code path, smallest reproduction, and available tests.
outputs: Focused regression test and smallest production fix when practical.
Evidence report naming failing-before and passing-after checks, failure output, nearby validation, or why failure evidence could not be demonstrated.
ordinaryExample: For an incorrect empty-input result with an existing local unit test, add the intended-behavior assertion, run it and observe the failure, fix the implementation, then run the same test and report the passing result.
capabilityLimits: Unavailable or denied execution leaves the proposed red-green sequence unrun.
Impractical tests use the closest useful regression check; do not force broad setup or brittle mocks.
Preserve disable-model-invocation metadata without assuming host enforcement.
Host behavior has not been tested.
